chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabala and Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Jamil, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The divorce of the pregnant woman is one (revocation). So when she gives birth to what is in her belly, she is irrevocably divorced.

key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: One (referring to a single revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period end for a pregnant woman who is divorced?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a pregnant woman's iddah consists of a single irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in), with the waiting period concluding immediately upon the delivery of the child. This ruling is derived from the Quranic verse 65:4 and is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the finality of divorce and the duration of the waiting period for pregnant spouses.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, and Ha’far Bin Sama’at, from Jameel, from Ismail Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A divorce of the pregnant woman is once. So when she places what is in her belly (gives birth), so she is irrevocably divorced’.
en.sarwar: 3. Flumayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah and Ja‘far ibn Sama‘ah from Jamil from ’Isma‘il al-Ju‘fiy ’Isma‘il who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Divorce of a pregnant woman is one and when she gives birth to what is inside her, she becomes stranger to him.’”
